extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, academic publishers, and researchers involved in peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journal editors and publishers to recognize, prevent, and mitigate reviewer fatigue so as to preserve review quality and timeliness. Covers procedural changes, incentives, reviewer recruitment, training, workload distribution, and technology use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and recognition of reviewer fatigue
rubrics_metrics.description: “Reviewer fatigue” has been defined as the difficulty that an editor faces in recruiting reviewers, who may feel overwhelmed by receiving excessive invitations to evaluate manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track recruitment difficulty and indicators (decline reasons, time-to-accept, % of invites refused). Use surveys and reports (e.g., Global State of Peer Review) to monitor trends and recognize when interventions are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify review process and reduce complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals can simplify guidelines and reduce the complexity of the review process to make the process easy and quick for the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise, streamlined review forms/checklists; remove unnecessary administrative steps; avoid asking reviewers to perform tasks beyond core assessment (e.g., extensive formatting checks). Aim to lower time-per-review without sacrificing essential evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed, clear review guidelines focused on key aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing detailed and clear review guidelines can help reviewers focus on key aspects of the manuscript, making the process more efficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer explicit prompts about what to evaluate (significance, methodology, clarity, ethics), examples of constructive comments, and suggested lengths/levels of detail. Clear scope reduces uncertainty and speeds reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use technology (including AI) for initial assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilization of technology, including artificial intelligence, for initial assessments can make the process less time-consuming for reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply automated triage for scope/fit checks, plagiarism screening, basic reporting-statistics checks, or method completeness to reduce reviewer burden. Ensure human oversight and transparency about automated steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer flexible review timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Offering more flexible timelines for reviews can relieve the pressure and allow reviewers to provide more thoughtful feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow adjustable deadlines based on reviewer workload; permit reasonable extensions; match timeline expectations to manuscript complexity. Avoid overly aggressive default deadlines that prompt superficial assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal recognition of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal recognition in the form of listing reviewers or providing certificates can encourage participation from reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly acknowledge reviewers (annual lists, certificates, ORCID recognition), provide letters of service, or offer reviewer badges to increase motivation and reward voluntary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives and publisher-provided benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: While financial incentive is not the main motivation for reviewers, reduction/waiver of publishing fee or free access to databases is provided by some publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider non-monetary incentives such as fee waivers, discounts, free access to content/databases, or credits toward open-access charges. Use incentives selectively and transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actively recruit diverse reviewers including early-career researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively seeking diverse reviewers can alleviate the workload on individual reviewers and bring fresh perspectives to the review process. Tap early career researchers who may be eager to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand reviewer pool across career stage, geography, gender, and sub-specialty. Invite qualified early-career researchers (with mentorship/training) to increase capacity and diversity of viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reviewer training and workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Offering training workshops focused on the peer review process can equip young researchers with the skills needed to conduct thorough reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver training on constructive feedback, critical appraisal, ethical issues, and journal expectations. Pair novices with experienced reviewers or offer mentorship programs to build capability and confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribute reviews and monitor reviewer workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Just 10% of reviewers handle almost 50% of peer reviews which can lead to mental and emotional strain for reviewers. The limited pool of active reviewers can limit perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor how many reviews each reviewer completes; implement caps or opt-in frequency limits; diversify assignments to avoid over-reliance on a small subgroup. Use editorial boards and databases to widen assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match reviewers to manuscripts by expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Many scholars refuse to review because the article does not fall within their area of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve reviewer selection by better matching expertise and scope to reduce refusals and superficial reviews. Use keywords, past publications, and author-suggested reviewers carefully to ensure fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance maintaining rigor with preventing reviewer burnout
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must strike a delicate balance between maintaining the rigor of the review process and preventing reviewer fatigue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize core quality checks while avoiding unnecessary burdens. Consider triage screening, staged review (e.g., short initial reviews), or editorial assessments to preserve rigor without overtaxing reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge voluntary nature and importance of recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review has always been perceived as a voluntary service; absence of formal recognition diminishes the motivation of the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize reviewing as academic service in promotion criteria, provide formal acknowledgment, and communicate appreciation to sustain participation and morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address causes of superficial assessments (deadlines and workload)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pressure to meet the deadline may cause superficial assessments and potential errors affecting the quality of scientific publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigate by allowing flexible deadlines, simplifying tasks required of reviewers, and ensuring reviewers have protected time; monitor review quality and provide feedback to reviewers when assessments are superficial.
